fixPlan: Stop deriving permanent PCM unit length from a single container timestamp gap. Container duration and decoded sample count are different quantities.

secondaryIssues.unfilteredResampling: AudioFeatureExtractor.java:145–160 performs linear interpolation without anti-aliasing;48k->16k is every third sample. Desktop analysis/features.py:634–650 delegates to FFmpeg filtered resampling.
secondaryIssues.rollingPercentile: AudioFeatureExtractor.java:326–329 uses weights upper-position and position-lower; both are0 for integer quantile positions. Startup count1,6,...196 yields false0 noise floors; fixed200sample window is unaffected.

assembler.productionImpact: Same NativeAudioDecoder and AudioFeatureExtractor are used by the production ensemble and neural pipelines. Production is subject to audio input drift for affected source timing; this is not a distilled model architecture issue.

savedFeatureAlignment.secondaryConfirmedCodeIssue: AudioFeatureExtractor.rollingPercentile multiplies equal floor/ceil endpoint by zero weights when quantile position is integral; happens at startup window sizes1,6,...196 and does not explain later-recording timing compression.
savedFeatureAlignment.method: Read-only frozen saved tensors and source code. No retraining, recalibration, new model selection, device invocation, or video extraction.

warp.source: Code-derived1106/1024 packet/frame ratio; no fitted slope oroffset
warp.orientation: Desktop time corresponding to native feature time t is t*1106/1024. To compare a native feature at t, interpolate desktop feature at t*1106/1024. Only compare where that desktop timestamp is within the recorded duration.
warp.interpretation: The feature assigned to10:00 contains sound from approximately10:48. By native16:22.5 the audio is exhausted; remaining78.5s repeat the last feature values.

savedFeatureAlignment.scope: A fixed time warp demonstrates the timeline defect; it does not create a corrected native extractor or qualify complete feature parity. Residual resampling/DSP differences remain.

samePcmReplay.scope: Offline 60-second excerpt. Same FFmpeg-decoded mono48k source PCM for all arms. Same16k PCM Java/Python isolates DSP; mono48k Java versus samePCM FFmpeg16k includes resampling difference. No phone, training, app change or deployment claim.
interpretation: Same16k PCM fed to Java and Python gives essentially identical steady-state DSP outputs after the first10seconds. Across all nonconstant audio columns, the minimum Pearson correlation is recorded in summary.

Known integer-percentile startup defect causes large transient noise-floor/SNR deviations during the first10seconds. These disappear in steady state. Ranking ties may amplify tiny floating-point differences in a small number of columns.

Using identical mono48k source PCM, native linear resampling versus FFmpeg filtered resampling retains near-unity RMS and low-band correlations on this excerpt; highest-band SNR differs more. This secondary mismatch cannot explain the very weak full-phone RMS and low-band correlations observed previously.

This test bypasses Android MediaCodec and its batched access-unit assembly. It isolates downstream DSP/resampling and supports investigating the independently identified access-unit timeline defect as the dominant cause. It is not a proof of repaired device inference or general audio-decoder parity.
One60second source excerpt; no full-media PCM decode, phone run, model inference, fitting, calibration or app mutation was performed in this replay.
